lesson.subtitle: Lesson 4 -- Under the City: Where Everything Is
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Giovanna de Fátima | Lesson 4 -- Under the City: Where Everything Is
lesson.grammar_point: prepositions of place and movement (through, along, across, into, under, above, between) over there is / there are

listenings.text: Good morning, everyone. This is Ray Collins with the plan for today. Listen carefully, because the north area is closed all week. Come in through the main gate, not through the small entrance on the west side. After the gate, walk along the fence, on the yellow walkway, never on the road. You pass three containers on your right. Our office is the second one, at ground level. The ramp into the tunnel is behind the containers, and nobody goes down there before eight. Thank you, and have a safe shift.

Hi Giovanna, it is Karen. You asked me what my site looks like from above, so here it is. Imagine a big grey rectangle with a blue fence around it. There is one entrance for people and one gate for the trucks, fifty meters away. Inside, there are two areas: the office area, with four containers, and the work area, with the machines. A yellow walkway goes across the middle, from the entrance to the ramp. And then the interesting part is underground. The tunnel runs under the street, twenty meters below our feet. I never see it from my window, but it is there, and my crew is in it right now.

extra_audio.text: Giovanna comes in through the main gate. She walks along the fence, on the yellow walkway. She goes across the yard and into the office container. After the meeting she walks down the ramp. Twenty meters underground, she inspects the tunnel wall.

defs: a narrow safe path for people, never for machines
a big metal box used as an office or a store on a site

a road that goes up or down, instead of steps
below the surface of the street
the place where you go into a building or a site

paras: From the tenth floor, the site is a grey rectangle in the middle of the city. There is a blue fence around it, and there is only one way in for people: a small entrance on the west side. The trucks do not use it. They come in through the big gate, fifty meters away.

Inside the fence there are two areas. On the left there is the office area: four white containers, two on the ground and two above them. The meeting room is at ground level, and the drawings are on the first floor. On the right there is the work area, with the machines, and nobody walks there without a helmet.
A yellow walkway goes across the site, from the entrance to the ramp. The rule is simple: people walk along the yellow line, machines use the road. There is no third way.

And then there is the part that nobody sees from the tenth floor. The ramp goes down, under the fence, under the road, into the tunnel. Twenty meters under the city, the crew works all day. Above them there are buses, cars and thousands of people who never think about the tunnel at all.
